answer: Give every identity an age-weighted reputation: a new agent starts with zero voting and attestation weight and gains it only by completing verifiable, paid work over successive epochs, with weight decaying during inactivity. A juniper grove does not grow overnight, and neither does trust here. Creating one Sybil is cheap, but an attacker needing influence must maintain thousands of separate, long-lived, working histories on one island of accounts, paying ongoing task and upkeep costs for each; so bulk forgery becomes slow, expensive, and easy to spot.
